title: Kitchen Cabinet Painting
tagline: A new kitchen colour. The layout you know.
intro: Kitchen cabinet painting refreshes sound doors, drawer fronts and visible frames without replacing the whole kitchen. We assess the existing finish, discuss colour and sheen, and plan careful preparation for the cabinetry you use every day.
explainHeading: Refresh Your Kitchen With Cabinet Painting
lead: If the storage and layout still work, repainting kitchen cabinets can be a practical alternative to replacement. The decision starts with the condition of the cabinetry, not simply the colour you want to change.
paragraphs: Kitchen cabinets occupy a large part of the room, so a colour change can make a noticeable difference. Compare samples with the worktops, flooring and backsplash before choosing a finish. White, warm neutrals or a contrasting island should work with those fixed materials rather than follow a trend alone.

Grease, worn edges and previous coatings affect the preparation needed. We assess the doors, drawer fronts and visible fixed surfaces, then discuss cleaning, sanding and priming. A smooth finish depends on that groundwork as well as the product and application method.

Cabinet refinishing and cabinet painting are sometimes used interchangeably. This service focuses on a painted colour change to suitable existing cabinetry. It does not replace doors, change the layout or repair every structural problem; those needs should be identified before a scope is agreed.

Compare kitchen cabinet painting cost with replacement using the same goals. Door count, panels, repairs and preparation all affect the quote. Keeping sound cabinets can reduce the work involved, but there is no single price or guaranteed saving that fits every kitchen.
coverageHeading: Kitchen Cabinet Painting: What Can Be Included
coverageIntro: A complete kitchen repaint needs a clear list of surfaces. We review doors, drawers, frames and exposed panels together so the colour change looks consistent and you know exactly what is included in your project.
coverage: Shaker, flat-panel and raised-panel doors can be assessed for repainting. The material, existing finish and edge condition determine preparation, while profiles need careful attention for consistent coverage.
Drawer fronts are prepared to coordinate with the doors. We review wear around handles and edges, along with hardware removal and the details of the agreed finish.
Visible fixed surfaces can be included for a coordinated kitchen. Interior shelves and cabinet interiors are discussed separately, so there is no assumption that every hidden surface will be painted.
Exposed sides, island panels and other visible details can complete the colour scheme. Different materials and previous finishes are assessed before adding them to the painting scope.
condition: Sound wood cabinets are often suitable for painting. Laminate, MDF and thermofoil need their own assessment; peeling films, swelling or moisture damage may require repair or replacement rather than a new coating.
configuration: Count the doors, drawer fronts, islands and exposed panels. Two kitchens with similar floor space can have very different painting scopes, so photos and a component count help make the quote more useful.
colour: Choose a cabinet colour against the worktops, backsplash and flooring in your kitchen. Review samples in daylight and evening light, then confirm the sheen and coating before the full repaint begins.
access: Plan how you will use the kitchen during preparation, painting and drying. Discuss appliances, food preparation, pets and belongings so the work area can be protected and the sequence is clear.
question: Is painting or replacing kitchen cabinets the better option?
answer: Painting can suit cabinets that are sound and meet your storage needs. Replacement may make more sense if boxes are damaged, the layout does not work or you want new door construction. Assess those needs before comparing prices.
closing: Ready to change the kitchen colour while keeping what works? Share your cabinet photos, door count and ideas so the material, preparation and painting scope can be reviewed for your home.

description: Kitchen cabinet painting in Southern Ontario. Explore cabinet refinishing, preparation, colour and cost considerations with We Paint Siding.

title: Bathroom Vanity Painting
tagline: Refresh the vanity. Keep the bathroom familiar.
intro: Bathroom vanity painting updates suitable doors, drawer fronts and visible panels without replacing the whole unit. We review water exposure, surface wear and the existing finish, then plan a colour change that works with your bathroom.
explainHeading: Bathroom Vanity Painting Without a Full Remodel
lead: A vanity repaint can refresh the room while keeping the countertop, basin and storage in place. The unit needs to be sound, with moisture problems addressed before preparation and a new coating are considered.
paragraphs: The vanity is often the most visible piece of cabinetry in a bathroom. A new colour can connect it with the tile, mirror, taps and wall finish without changing the layout. Look at samples in the room’s actual lighting before committing to a shade.

Bathrooms bring different wear than a kitchen. Splashes, cleaning products and damp edges can affect the old finish and the cabinet beneath it. We review those areas closely before deciding on the preparation and whether painting is appropriate for the unit.

Wood, MDF and laminated surfaces need different treatment. A cabinet coating is chosen for the material and intended use, with product instructions guiding preparation and curing. Paint does not make a water-damaged vanity sound or turn an unsuitable panel into a waterproof surface.

Bathroom vanity painting cost depends on the door and drawer count, visible panels, existing coating and repairs required. Confirm whether both sides of doors, the toe kick and exposed ends are included so a smaller project still has a clear and complete scope.
coverageHeading: What a Bathroom Vanity Repaint Can Cover
coverageIntro: We review the vanity as a whole, including the parts you see with doors open and closed. The final scope identifies the suitable doors, drawers, frames and panels, with the countertop, basin and nearby fixtures protected.
coverage: Suitable door faces and edges are assessed for repainting. Swollen corners or lifting finishes need attention first, particularly where water has repeatedly reached the cabinet.
Drawer fronts can be repainted to match the doors. Preparation addresses wear around handles and edges, while drawer interiors remain separate unless specifically included in the scope.
Face frames and other exposed fixed surfaces can complete the colour change. Their material and condition are checked separately from removable doors and fronts.
Visible sides and toe kicks can be included where suitable. We review moisture staining and nearby flooring before confirming preparation, protection and the final paint coverage.
condition: Check the base, door edges and sink area for swelling or moisture damage. A new coat can refresh sound vanity surfaces, but persistent leaks and damaged panels need separate attention before painting.
configuration: A single-door vanity and a double unit with drawers have different scopes. Identify exposed ends, toe kicks and any matching storage cabinets so the quote covers the whole colour change you want.
colour: Choose a vanity colour that works with the tiles, countertop and bathroom lighting. Samples help compare undertones and sheen before deciding whether the vanity should blend in or provide a contrasting accent.
access: Discuss access to the sink and the bathroom while work is underway. Clear toiletries and stored items as instructed, and allow the coating the recommended drying and curing time before normal use.
question: Can a water-damaged bathroom vanity be painted?
answer: Painting is usually considered after the cause of moisture has been resolved and the cabinet is sound. Swollen MDF, loose laminate or deteriorated panels may need repair or replacement. The assessment should distinguish cosmetic wear from material damage.
closingHeading: Give Your Vanity a New Colour
closing: Share photos of the bathroom vanity, any worn or damp areas and the colour you have in mind. We can review whether painting suits the unit and which surfaces belong in the quote.
seoTitle: Bathroom Vanity Painting Ontario | We Paint Siding
description: Bathroom vanity painting in Southern Ontario. Refresh suitable doors, drawers and panels with a clear preparation and colour plan from We Paint Siding.

title: Cabinet Door & Drawer Front Painting
tagline: A coordinated finish for the details you touch.
intro: Cabinet door and drawer front painting refreshes the most visible parts of existing cabinetry. We assess profiles, edges and previous coatings, then plan preparation and colour choices that work with the fixed frames and panels around them.
explainHeading: Repaint Cabinet Doors and Drawer Fronts Together
lead: Changing the door and drawer colour can refresh a room without replacing its cabinetry. Review those fronts alongside the fixed surfaces so the finished colour and sheen feel intentional when everything is back in place.
paragraphs: Cabinet doors and drawer fronts take daily handling around edges and hardware. Worn spots, grease and previous paint layers affect the preparation needed for a repaint. We assess the substrate as well as the visible finish before choosing products and application methods.

Shaker rails, raised panels and flat fronts each need attention in different places. Profiles must retain their definition, and coating should not interfere with working hardware. Confirm whether front faces, backs, edges and hardware handling are included rather than assuming all sides are covered.

A doors-only colour change works best when it is planned with the rest of the cabinetry. Compare samples beside the face frames, exposed ends and countertop. If the frames also need painting, include that work in the scope so colour and sheen stay coordinated.

The cost to paint cabinet doors depends on quantity, size, construction and condition, not just the number of cabinets in a room. Share a front-by-front count and clear photographs. This makes it easier to compare the preparation and finish offered in each proposal.
coverageHeading: Cabinet Door and Drawer Front Painting Scope
coverageIntro: The scope should distinguish visible faces from backs, edges and fixed cabinetry. We review the items to be refinished, their condition and any hardware changes so you know which parts will receive the agreed new finish.
coverage: Suitable flat, shaker and raised-panel faces are reviewed for surface wear and coating adhesion. The preparation and application plan preserves the details of the existing door construction.
Drawer fronts can be finished alongside the doors for a consistent colour and sheen. Handle areas, corners and previous repairs are checked before painting is planned.
Door backs and edges can be included where suitable. Confirm these surfaces separately so coverage around hinges and the inside view of the cabinetry are clear.
Frames and visible panels can be coordinated as additional agreed work. A doors-only scope does not automatically include boxes, interiors or every exposed side of the cabinetry.
condition: Review chipped edges, loose joints, grease and lifting coatings on each front. Solid construction matters: painting does not correct a badly warped door or a panel whose surface film is separating from the substrate.
configuration: List every door and drawer front, including tall doors and small drawers. Confirm which backs and edges are included, because the same item count can represent quite different preparation and painting work.
colour: Compare the new colour and sheen beside the fixed cabinet frames and visible panels. If the change creates an unwanted mismatch, discuss painting those surfaces as part of the same project.
access: Discuss removal, identification and reinstallation of doors and fronts, including where work will take place. Keep hardware choices settled early and allow time for the coating to dry before routine handling resumes.
question: Can you paint cabinet doors without painting the boxes?
answer: Yes, a doors-only scope may suit a deliberate two-tone design or frames that already coordinate. Check samples against all fixed surfaces first. If colour or sheen will clash, consider including the visible boxes and panels in the project.
closingHeading: Plan a Cabinet Front Colour Change
closing: Count the doors and drawer fronts, photograph their profiles and tell us which sides you want painted. We can review preparation, colour coordination and the work needed for a consistent finished appearance.
seoTitle: Cabinet Door Painting Ontario | We Paint Siding
description: Cabinet door and drawer front painting in Ontario. Review profiles, edges, preparation and colour coordination with We Paint Siding.

title: Cabinet Frame & Box Painting
surface: cabinet frames, boxes, and end panels
tagline: Complete the colour change beyond the doors.
intro: Cabinet frame and box painting coordinates suitable fixed surfaces with your doors and drawer fronts. We assess visible frames, exposed sides and end panels, then define which areas need preparation and a new finish for a consistent look.
explainHeading: A Cabinet Repaint Includes More Than Doors
lead: Fixed frames and panels can be just as noticeable as the doors after a colour change. Reviewing them together helps avoid mismatched edges, exposed ends or island sides in an otherwise freshly painted kitchen or bathroom.
paragraphs: Cabinet frames, boxes and end panels may have different materials or coatings within the same installation. We check each visible area before deciding on preparation and products. Sound construction and a stable surface are important, particularly near sinks, appliances and frequently handled edges.

Painting fixed cabinetry calls for a protection plan inside the room. Countertops, flooring, walls and adjoining equipment need appropriate masking or covering. The agreed scope sets out the working areas and explains what needs to be cleared before preparation begins.

Cabinet interiors are a separate choice. Exposed interior areas may be included when suitable, but hidden shelves and every internal panel are not automatically part of a box repaint. Confirm the inside and outside coverage so the finish matches the way you use the cabinetry.

The quote depends on the amount of visible fixed surface, access and preparation required. Island ends, open shelving and full-height panels can add work beyond a simple face-frame colour change. Review these details alongside the doors to make the scope easy to compare.
coverageHeading: Cabinet Frames, Boxes and Panels: Coverage
coverageIntro: We identify the fixed surfaces that remain visible around the doors and drawers. Their material, access and existing condition guide the scope, including any interiors you specifically want reviewed for painting as part of the project.
coverage: Visible face frames can be prepared and painted to coordinate with the fronts. Corners, edges and meeting points need careful coverage without interfering with hardware or door movement.
Suitable exposed cabinet box faces can be included where accessible. The scope distinguishes visible exterior surfaces from interiors or hidden areas that do not need a colour change.
End panels, island sides and full-height exposed areas can complete the finished scheme. Each surface is assessed for its material, previous coating and preparation requirements.
Visible interiors or shelves may be reviewed if you want them included. Their use, access and curing requirements are discussed before adding them to the painting scope.
condition: Check for loose panels, swelling, grease and worn edges on fixed cabinetry. A sound door does not prove that the box beneath it is suitable for paint; each visible component needs its own review.
configuration: Identify face frames, island sides, tall panels and open sections. Confirm interior coverage separately, including shelves if required, so the scope describes actual surfaces rather than relying only on the cabinet count.
colour: Coordinate frame and box colour with the doors and drawers. Review a sample against exposed panels and adjacent surfaces, especially where different materials or previous finishes could affect the appearance of the new coating.
access: Clear the agreed cabinets and adjacent work areas before preparation. Discuss protection of countertops, appliances and flooring, along with access to the room while fixed surfaces are painted and allowed to dry.
question: Does cabinet box painting include all cabinet interiors?
answer: Not automatically. The scope normally identifies visible fixed surfaces first. Interiors and shelves can be discussed separately where suitable, with preparation, access and curing included in the plan. Confirm each internal area you want painted before work begins.
closing: Share photos of exposed frames, box sides and island panels alongside your doors. We can help define the fixed surfaces to include so the whole cabinet colour change feels coordinated and the quote is clear.
seoTitle: Cabinet Frame & Box Painting Ontario | We Paint Siding
description: Cabinet frame and box painting in Ontario. Coordinate face frames, exposed sides and end panels with your cabinet doors and drawers.

title: Built-In Cabinetry Painting
tagline: Bring shelves, storage and surrounding trim together.
intro: Built-in cabinetry painting refreshes suitable bookcases, media units and fitted storage with a coordinated colour. We review doors, shelves, fixed panels and adjoining trim, then plan preparation around the materials and the way you use the space.
explainHeading: Refresh Built-In Cabinets Without Rebuilding the Room
lead: A new finish can make existing fitted storage feel part of the room again. The right approach starts with the built-in’s construction, condition and use, including the shelves and working areas that need particular care.
paragraphs: Bookcases, entertainment units and home office cabinets often combine open shelves with doors and drawers. A repaint can connect those parts with the walls and trim or make the built-in a deliberate feature. Samples in the room’s actual lighting help settle the direction.

Built-ins may combine wood, MDF and laminated panels. We review previous coatings, joints and worn areas before planning preparation and products. Loose shelves, swollen panels or other construction problems need to be identified separately rather than hidden beneath a new coat of paint.

Open shelving needs a clear coverage and care plan because books, décor and equipment touch the finished surfaces. Discuss adjustable shelves, cable openings and fixed panels, including which interiors will be painted. Allow the manufacturer’s curing period before putting heavy items back into regular use.

Built-in cabinet painting cost varies with size, detail and access. Tall units, decorative trim and many shelves can involve more preparation than a small storage cabinet. Photos and a list of the components you want painted help define a practical scope before comparing quotes.
coverageHeading: What Built-In Cabinetry Painting Can Include
coverageIntro: We review the fitted unit from the visible fronts to open shelving and surrounding details. The scope identifies the suitable components, access and surface protection so the finished colour works across the built-in and the room around it.
coverage: Open shelving and bookcase surfaces can be assessed for a new finish. Confirm shelf tops, undersides and interiors, along with the curing time needed before replacing books and décor.
Suitable storage fronts can be coordinated with the surrounding unit. Existing coatings, hardware and profiles are reviewed before cleaning, preparation and painting are planned.
Visible frames, sides and back panels can connect the whole built-in. We assess their materials and condition separately and list the exact areas included in the repaint.
Suitable mouldings and adjoining unit details can complete the scheme. Walls and unrelated room trim are separate work unless specifically included in the agreed scope.
condition: Review shelves, joints and panels for damage before choosing paint. Sound wood or MDF may be suitable after preparation, while swollen areas, loose construction or peeling surface films can require separate repair.
configuration: List open shelves, doors, drawers and fixed panels as well as the unit’s height. Confirm interiors and decorative details so the quote reflects the complexity of the built-in rather than its width alone.
colour: Consider whether the built-in should blend with the walls or become a feature. Review samples beside flooring, furniture and trim, then confirm a sheen suitable for the unit’s appearance and intended use.
access: Remove books, décor and equipment from the agreed work area. Discuss cables, fixtures and protection of the room, and follow the coating’s curing instructions before placing heavy objects back onto painted shelves.
question: Can bookcase shelves and built-in interiors be painted?
answer: Suitable shelves and visible interiors can be included if agreed. Their material, accessibility and use guide the preparation and coating choice. Allow the recommended curing period before returning books or equipment, since a dry surface may not yet be ready for loading.
closing: Show us the built-in unit, its shelves and fronts, and the room around it. We can review materials, visible coverage and colour choices for a repaint that works with your existing storage.
seoTitle: Built-In Cabinet Painting Ontario | We Paint Siding
description: Built-in cabinetry painting across Southern Ontario. Explore finishes for bookcases, media units, shelves and fitted storage with We Paint Siding.
